questions.question: When an owner deletes a document, is it gone for good or can it be restored, and for how long? What should colleagues who had access to it see afterwards?
questions.why_it_matters: Delete is one of the four actions you confirmed, and the trash icon sits next to Share, so a mis-click is plausible. Colleagues the owner shared with could lose work without warning. The answer also decides whether delete needs a confirmation step or an undo.

options.option: Permanent delete with a confirmation naming the document
options.trade_offs: Simplest to build and no storage kept. A mis-click cannot be undone, and colleagues lose the document immediately. The confirmation click may count towards the two-click limit.

options.option: Recoverable delete (trash for a set period) with an undo control and no confirmation
options.trade_offs: Protects against mis-clicks and fits the two-click limit. Needs a retention period, a restore action, and a decision on whether shares come back on restore. Deleted documents keep using storage.

options.option: Recoverable delete that also asks for confirmation when the document is shared with others
options.trade_offs: Extra protection for shared documents, which others rely on. More states to build, and shared deletes take an extra click.

questions.question: What may a colleague do with a document shared as viewer, and what may one shared as editor do?
questions.why_it_matters: You asked for viewer and editor roles like Google Drive but not what each role can do. Without this, we cannot say whether an editor may rename, delete or re-share the owner's document, which affects your requirement that only people the owner chooses can open it. It also decides whether shared documents appear in the Documents list.

options.option: Viewer can open and download; editor can also change content but cannot rename, delete or re-share
options.trade_offs: Keeps the owner fully in control, matching the 'only the owner manages' rule. Editors cannot tidy or reorganise the document.

options.option: Editor can also rename and upload new versions, but only the owner can delete or re-share
options.trade_offs: More useful for teamwork. Names and versions can change without the owner knowing.

options.option: Editor can do everything except change who has access, including delete
options.trade_offs: Closest to full collaboration, but a colleague can remove a document the owner relies on. This conflicts with the owner-only rule for managing documents.

questions.question: When an owner shares or revokes access, what should they see, and how can they check who currently has access?
questions.why_it_matters: Sharing and revoking are the only way your security rule is applied, yet the captured screens show only a Share button. Owners need to choose the right colleague and be sure that revoked access has really been removed.

options.option: A share window listing current colleagues with their role, a remove control, and a confirmation message after each change
options.trade_offs: Owners can see and correct access at any time and know a revoke worked. More screens and messages to design and test.

options.option: A share window only for adding colleagues, with revoke available elsewhere and a brief message
options.trade_offs: Less to build, but owners cannot easily see who has access, so a wrong share may go unnoticed.

questions.question: How do employees sign in today, and where should the list of colleagues that owners share with come from?
questions.why_it_matters: The feature is for signed-in employees and owners choose named colleagues, but no sign-in or employee directory has been identified. This also fixes whether sharing is limited to employees of your organisation.

options.option: Use an existing company sign-in and employee directory (please name it)
options.trade_offs: Employees keep one login and the colleague list stays current. Depends on access to that system and its rules.

options.option: Build a new user list for this feature
options.trade_offs: Independent of other systems. Someone must maintain the list, and it can drift from who actually works for you.

questions.question: When an employee leaves or their account is deactivated, what should happen to their documents and the access they granted? Can ownership be transferred?
questions.why_it_matters: Only the owner can manage a document and who can open it. If the owner leaves, shared documents could be orphaned, stay accessible to no one, or be kept forever.

options.option: Transfer ownership to another named employee, such as a manager
options.trade_offs: Shared work stays available. Needs a transfer step and someone to decide the new owner.

options.option: Delete the leaver's documents and remove all shares
options.trade_offs: Simple and nothing is kept indefinitely. Colleagues lose documents they depend on.

options.option: Keep documents and shares as they are, read-only, until someone deletes them
options.trade_offs: Nothing is lost immediately. No one can manage access, and documents may be retained indefinitely.

questions.question: For the 'at most two clicks' rule, where does counting start, and do steps like choosing a colleague, choosing viewer or editor, or confirming a delete count as clicks?
questions.why_it_matters: Sharing needs a colleague and a role, and delete may need a confirmation. Depending on how clicks are counted these may not fit in two clicks, and the rule cannot be tested without a counting rule.

options.option: Count from the document row, and count every click including choices and confirmations
options.trade_offs: Strictest reading and easiest to test. Sharing probably cannot fit in two clicks, so the rule may need to be relaxed for it.

options.option: Count only the clicks that start and complete the action; choosing a colleague or role by typing or selection does not count
options.trade_offs: Realistic for sharing. Less strict, so the test needs a clear written definition.

options.option: Apply two clicks to upload, rename and delete only; sharing gets its own target
options.trade_offs: Honest about the extra steps sharing needs. Changes your original wording for sharing.

implementation_details.item: Rename rules: validation, duplicate names and file extension, and where the rename control appears
Upload rules: allowed types, size limit, multiple files, duplicate names, progress and failure messages
Document list at 1,000 items: default sort, paging and search, and how the two-second target is measured
Empty, loading, success and error states and how they are announced
Accessible names for the icon-only delete button and unlabeled actions column
Notices to colleagues when access is granted or revoked
What a colleague sees if access is revoked or the document is deleted while it is open
Optional history of share, revoke and delete actions
Optional monitoring of page load times against the two-second target
